```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r load-data}
#| include: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Flux data from Block 4
source("scripts/read_hh.R")
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
cache_file <- "data/processed/all_hh.rds"
if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
  all_hh <- readRDS(cache_file)
} else {
  zips   <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
  all_hh <- bind_rows(lapply(zips, read_hh))
  saveRDS(all_hh, cache_file)
}

# Block 5 datasets
soil   <- read_csv("data/external/soilgrids/soilgrids_my_sites.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
traits <- read_csv("data/external/planttraits/planttraits_my_sites.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Data and provenance

Five external datasets were added to the FLUXNET data from Block 4. All were
downloaded with the Block 5 scripts and are stored in `data/external/`.

```{r provenance}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Dataset,          ~Source,                                ~Resolution,              ~Period,                  ~`Accessed`,   ~Citation,
  "FLUXNET (ONEFlux v1.3)", "FLUXNET Shuttle (AmeriFlux, ICOS)", "tower, 30 min",        "tower years (1999–2025)", "2026-11-13", "Site citations (see Block 4); Pastorello et al. (2020)",
  "SoilGrids 2.0",   "ISRIC, rest.isric.org",                "250 m, 6 depths",        "static",                 "2026-11-20", "Poggio et al. (2021) SOIL 7, 217–240",
  "PlantTraits",     "planttraits.earth / Zenodo",           "1 km",                   "static",                 "2026-11-20", "Lusk et al. (2026) Nat. Commun. 17, 1203; doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14646322",
  "WorldClim 2.1",   "worldclim.org (via geodata)",          "5′ (~9 km)",             "1970–2000 normals",      "2026-11-20", "Fick & Hijmans (2017) Int. J. Climatol. 37, 4302–4315",
  "iNaturalist",     "api.inaturalist.org/v1",               "points, 5 km radius",    "all records to date",    "2026-11-20", "iNaturalist contributors (2026), accessed 2026-11-20",
  "MODIS MOD13Q1",   "ORNL DAAC subset service",             "250 m, 16 days (9 × 9 px)", "last 3 tower years",   "2026-11-23", "Didan (2021) doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061; ORNL DAAC doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/1557"
```

## 2. Site portrait

All values come from `data/processed/site_static.csv` (built by
`09_merge.R`). Soil values are thickness-weighted means over 0–30 cm.

```{r portrait-data}
site_static <- read_csv("data/processed/site_static.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

### Climate (WorldClim 2.1, 1970–2000)

```{r portrait-climate}
site_static |>
      mutate(lat = paste0(abs(round(lat, 2)), "° ", if_else(lat < 0, "S", "N")),
         lon = paste0(abs(round(lon, 2)), "° ", if_else(lon < 0, "W", "E"))) |>
  select(Site = site_id, IGBP = igbp,
        Lat = lat, Lon = lon,
         `BIO1 mean temp. (°C)` = BIO1,
         `BIO4 temp. seasonality (°C × 100)` = BIO4,
         `BIO12 annual precip. (mm)` = BIO12,
         `BIO15 precip. seasonality (%)` = BIO15) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The WorldClim annual precipitation (BIO12) confirms the problem found in
Block 4: P_F from FLUXNET is about four times higher than BIO12 at US-UiB
and about three times higher at CN-Zha, while it is close to BIO12 at the
other three towers.

### Soil (SoilGrids 2.0, 0–30 cm)

```{r portrait-soil}
site_static |>
  mutate(CN = soil0_30_soc / soil0_30_nitrogen) |>
  select(Site = site_id,
         `Clay (%)` = soil0_30_clay, `Sand (%)` = soil0_30_sand,
         `Silt (%)` = soil0_30_silt,
         `SOC (g/kg)` = soil0_30_soc, `N (g/kg)` = soil0_30_nitrogen,
         `C:N (-)` = CN, `pH (-)` = soil0_30_phh2o,
         `Bulk density (kg/dm³)` = soil0_30_bdod,
         `CEC (cmol(c)/kg)` = soil0_30_cec) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

### Plant traits (PlantTraits, community-weighted means) and species records (iNaturalist, 5 km)

```{r portrait-plants}
site_static |>
  select(Site = site_id,
         `SLA (m²/kg)` = SLA,
         `Leaf N mass (mg/g)` = leaf_N_mass,
         `Leaf N area (g/m²)` = leaf_N_area,
         `Stem density (g/cm³)` = stem_density,
         `Rooting depth (m)` = rooting_depth,
         `Leaf area (mm²)` = leaf_area,
         `Plant height* (m)` = plant_height,
         `Observations (n)` = n_obs,
         `Species (n)` = n_species,
         `Plant species (n)` = n_plant_species) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

\* Plant height is an experimental map (cross-validated r < 0.5). The
PlantTraits area-of-applicability flag is 0 for all traits at all towers
(see Section 4). Species counts are not comparable between towers: they
depend on how many people observe near each tower, not only on biodiversity.
At US-UiB, the script retrieved only 3,000 of 26,911 observations, so its
species counts are underestimated.

## 3. Greenness and GPP

NDVI and EVI were computed from the MODIS MOD13Q1 red, NIR and blue
reflectances (own values) and compared with the NDVI and EVI products
delivered by MODIS. Both use the same 9 × 9 pixel window (about 2 × 2 km)
around each tower and only pixels with reliability 0 (good) or 1 (marginal).
The MODIS product bands were not included in the course script and were
downloaded separately (`scripts/block5/08b_modis_product_vi.R`). MODIS covers
the last three years of each tower record.

```{r vi-data}
modis_own  <- read_csv("data/external/modis/modis_vi_my_sites.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
modis_prod <- read_csv("data/external/modis/modis_product_vi_my_sites.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

vi <- modis_own |>
  select(site_id, date, own_ndvi = ndvi, own_evi = evi) |>
  inner_join(modis_prod, by = c("site_id", "date"))

# Check: eigene Werte gegen MODIS-Produkt
vi |>
  summarise(`Dates`             = n(),
            `r NDVI`            = cor(own_ndvi, modis_ndvi, use = "complete.obs"),
            `Mean abs. diff. NDVI (-)` = mean(abs(own_ndvi - modis_ndvi), na.rm = TRUE),
            `r EVI`             = cor(own_evi, modis_evi, use = "complete.obs"),
            `Mean abs. diff. EVI (-)`  = mean(abs(own_evi - modis_evi), na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = site_id) |>
  rename(Site = site_id) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r vi-figure}
#| fig-cap: "Daily GPP (top) and NDVI and EVI (bottom) for each tower over the MODIS period. Own values (filled) and MODIS products (open) overlap almost exactly."
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 12
# Tägliche GPP aus den Block-4-Daten (mit VUT/CUT- und NT/DT-Ersatz)
gpp_daily <- all_hh |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time)) |>
  summarise(GPP = mean(GPP) * 1.0378, .by = c(site, date)) |>
  rename(site_id = site)

rng <- vi |> summarise(start = min(date), end = max(date), .by = site_id)

gpp_plot <- gpp_daily |>
  inner_join(rng, by = "site_id") |>
  filter(date >= start, date <= end) |>
  mutate(panel = "GPP (g C/m²/d)")

vi_long <- vi |>
  pivot_longer(c(own_ndvi, own_evi, modis_ndvi, modis_evi),
               names_to = c("source", "index"), names_sep = "_") |>
  mutate(index  = toupper(index),
         source = if_else(source == "own", "Own", "MODIS"),
         panel  = "NDVI / EVI (-)")

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = gpp_plot, aes(date, GPP), colour = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = vi_long, aes(date, value, colour = index, shape = source),
             size = 1.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ site_id, scales = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Own = 16, MODIS = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = NULL, colour = "Index", shape = "Source") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", legend.position = "top",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
Own and MODIS NDVI agree exactly (r = 1) at all towers; EVI agrees almost
exactly (r ≥ 0.999). At US-UiB, no GPP is available for the MODIS period
(2022–2024), because GPP and RECO are missing after about 2022 at this site.
IT-Tor has the fewest valid dates (44), as many winter scenes are flagged as
snow or cloud and removed.

## 4. My question: soil C:N and light-use efficiency

**Question.** Is the topsoil C:N ratio related to ecosystem light-use
efficiency (LUE) during the peak growing season across my five towers?

**Hypothesis.** Sites with a lower C:N ratio (more available nitrogen) have a
higher LUE, because more nitrogen allows more photosynthetic capacity per leaf.

**Method.** Topsoil C:N is the ratio of soil organic carbon to total nitrogen
from SoilGrids, thickness-weighted over 0–30 cm. LUE is the sum of daily GPP
(g C m⁻² d⁻¹) divided by the sum of daily incoming shortwave radiation
SW_IN_F (MJ m⁻² d⁻¹) over the three months with the highest mean GPP at each
site. Leaf nitrogen per mass from PlantTraits is shown as a second possible
link between soil and photosynthesis.

```{r q-data}
# Topsoil 0–30 cm, gewichtet nach Schichtdicke
soil_top <- soil |>
  filter(top_cm < 30) |>
  mutate(w = bottom_cm - top_cm) |>
  summarise(value = weighted.mean(mean, w), .by = c(site_id, property)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = property, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(CN = soc / nitrogen)

# Tageswerte
daily <- all_hh |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time)) |>
  summarise(GPP = mean(GPP) * 1.0378,       # g C m⁻² d⁻¹
            SW  = mean(SW_IN_F) * 0.0864,   # MJ m⁻² d⁻¹
            .by = c(site, date)) |>
  mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")))

# Die drei Monate mit der höchsten mittleren GPP
peak <- daily |>
  summarise(gpp_month = mean(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, month)) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  slice_max(gpp_month, n = 3) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(site, month)

# Lichtnutzungseffizienz
lue <- daily |>
  semi_join(peak, by = c("site", "month")) |>
  filter(!is.na(GPP), !is.na(SW)) |>
  summarise(LUE         = sum(GPP) / sum(SW),
            n_days      = n(),
            peak_months = paste(sort(unique(month)), collapse = ", "),
            .by = site) |>
  rename(site_id = site)

q <- lue |>
  left_join(soil_top |> select(site_id, soc, nitrogen, CN), by = "site_id") |>
  left_join(traits |> select(site_id, leaf_N_mass, leaf_N_mass_aoa), by = "site_id") |>
  arrange(CN)

q |>
  select(Site = site_id,
         `SOC (g kg⁻¹)` = soc, `N (g kg⁻¹)` = nitrogen, `C:N (–)` = CN,
         `Leaf N (mg g⁻¹)` = leaf_N_mass, `Leaf N AOA` = leaf_N_mass_aoa,
         `Peak months` = peak_months, `Days` = n_days,
         `LUE (g C MJ⁻¹)` = LUE) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```
The PlantTraits area-of-applicability flag (`_aoa`) is 0 for all traits at all
five towers. It is not yet clear whether 0 means inside or outside the area of
applicability; the leaf N values should therefore be read with caution.
```{r q-figure}
#| fig-cap: "Peak-season light-use efficiency against topsoil C:N (SoilGrids, 0–30 cm) and community leaf nitrogen (PlantTraits). n = 5 towers."
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 9
q |>
  select(site_id, LUE,
         `Topsoil C:N (-)` = CN,
         `Leaf N (mg/g)` = leaf_N_mass) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(site_id, LUE), names_to = "driver") |>
  ggplot(aes(value, LUE, label = site_id)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 3.5, box.padding = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ driver, scales = "free_x", strip.position = "bottom") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.15)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.15)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression("Peak-season LUE (g C MJ"^-1*")")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside")
```

The figure does not support the hypothesis. BR-Ma2 shows the highest LUE,
although it has the second-highest C:N ratio (about 13). The lowest LUE, in
contrast, occurs at IT-Tor, which also has the highest C:N ratio (about 15).
Both the low LUE and the high soil carbon content at IT-Tor can be explained
by the characteristics of this alpine site: the short growing season and low
temperatures limit photosynthesis as well as the microbial decomposition of
organic matter, so carbon accumulates in the soil. It is therefore likely that
any nitrogen signal is masked by more dominant climate controls.
With only five towers (n = 5) in very different climates, this comparison is
descriptive and cannot test a statistical relationship; differences in
vegetation type, management (e.g. fertilisation at the US-UiB cropland) and
partitioning method (DT at BR-Ma2, NT elsewhere) may also affect LUE.
In addition, the low soil carbon, low C:N and high pH (8.4) at CN-Zha suggest
that the 250 m SoilGrids pixel represents the surrounding dry soils rather
than the wetland itself. Testing the hypothesis properly would require more
towers within a similar climate, for example using the data of the whole class.

## 5. Scale

The flux footprint, the area the tower actually measures, is roughly
100 m to 1 km. The external datasets see very different areas:

```{r scale}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Dataset,       ~`Pixel / area`,             ~`Compared with footprint`, ~`What it means for my answer`,
  "SoilGrids",    "250 m",                     "similar",                  "Right scale for C:N, but a model prediction; at CN-Zha the pixel seems to show the dry surroundings (pH 8.4, low SOC), not the wetland.",
  "PlantTraits",  "1 km",                      "similar to larger",        "Mixes vegetation types around the tower; croplands and wetlands are poorly covered; AOA unclear.",
  "MODIS",        "250 m, 9 × 9 px (~2 × 2 km)", "larger",                 "The window includes land cover around the tower (other fields at US-UiB, desert/oasis at CN-Zha); greenness is not only the footprint.",
  "WorldClim",    "5′ (~9 km)",                "much larger",              "Regional climate only; in mountains (IT-Tor, JP-Fhk) one cell mixes very different elevations.",
  "iNaturalist",  "5 km radius",               "much larger",              "Records cluster along roads and towns; counts describe observers as much as species."
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

For my question, the most important scale issue is SoilGrids: the 250 m
pixel matches the footprint in size, but at CN-Zha it probably does not
represent the wetland soil. The C:N value used for this tower is therefore
uncertain. LUE itself comes from the tower and represents the footprint.

## Data and citation

**Time zone.** FLUXNET days are local standard time (no daylight saving).
MODIS dates are the start dates of the 16-day composites. ERA5-Land was not
used in this report.

**FLUXNET site data.** Each site's data citation from the FLUXNET Shuttle
snapshot:

```{r citations}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
snapshot_file <- list.files("data/snapshots", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)[1]
read_csv(snapshot_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(site_id %in% site_static$site_id) |>
  distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(line = paste0("- **", site_id, "**: ", product_citation)) |>
  pull(line) |>
  cat(sep = "\n")
```

- Pastorello, G. et al. (2020): The FLUXNET2015 dataset and the ONEFlux
  processing pipeline for eddy covariance data. *Scientific Data* 7, 225.
  <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3>

**External datasets** (access dates in Section 1):

- **SoilGrids 2.0:** Poggio, L. et al. (2021): SoilGrids 2.0: producing soil
  information for the globe with quantified spatial uncertainty. *SOIL* 7,
  217–240. Data: ISRIC, soilgrids.org.
- **PlantTraits:** Lusk et al. (2026), *Nature Communications* 17, 1203.
  Data: planttraits.earth, <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14646322>.
- **WorldClim 2.1:** Fick, S. E. & Hijmans, R. J. (2017): WorldClim 2: new
  1-km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas.
  *International Journal of Climatology* 37, 4302–4315. Data: worldclim.org.
- **iNaturalist:** iNaturalist contributors (2026), research-grade
  observations accessed via api.inaturalist.org/v1 on 2026-11-20.
- **MODIS MOD13Q1:** Didan, K. (2021): MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day
  L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061. NASA LP DAAC,
  <https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061>. Accessed through the ORNL DAAC
  MODIS subset service, <https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/1557>.
